review_notes: Codex exhaustively reviewed the paper’s eight-sentence scientific Abstract, excluding the separate Simple Summary. Negative HGF results, in-vitro and in-vivo settings, unspecified direction of MET-ablation effects, and procedure/method claims are represented. The two instruction profiles share one source paper and are not independent documents. These are Codex labels, not independent human labels. The first frozen held-out offline probe is preserved at out/met-axis-first-offline.json (2/17 focused and 2/23 unfocused candidates). These fixtures moved to development before extraction changed and cannot count toward the final held-out test. The phrase in vitro qualifies the whole ineffective-stimulation finding, including intracellular signaling.
text: Cancer cell dissemination is sustained by cell-autonomous and non-cell-autonomous functions. To disentangle the role of HGF (Hepatocyte Growth Factor) and MET ligand/receptor axis in this complex process, we genetically knocked out the MET gene in cancer cells in which MET is not the oncogenic driver. In this way, we evaluated the contribution of the HGF/MET axis to cancer cell dissemination independently of its direct activities in cells of the tumor microenvironment. The lack of MET expression in MET−/− cells has been proved by molecular characterization. From a functional point of view, HGF stimulation of MET−/− cancer cells was ineffective in eliciting intracellular signaling and in sustaining biological functions predictive of malignancy in vitro (i.e., anchorage-independent growth, invasion, and survival in the absence of matrix adhesion). Cancer cell dissemination was assessed in vivo, evaluating: (i) the ability of MET−/− lung carcinoma cells to colonize the lungs following intravenous injection and (ii) the spontaneous dissemination to distant organs of MET−/− pancreatic carcinoma cells upon orthotopic injection. In both experimental models, MET ablation affects the time of onset, the number, and the size of metastatic lesions. These results define a crucial contribution of the HGF/MET axis to cell-autonomous functions driving the metastatic process.
